description: Hi everyone! I am a beginner programmer looking to learn, collaborate, and push myself during this challenge. I am taking on the Team Lead role to manage our schedule, coordinate tasks, and help with documentation. I am looking for enthusiastic teammates of all skill levels—especially anyone with coding, data analysis, or design experience—who want to learn together and build a cool project.
summary:
Project Next Generation Astronauts is a game that simulates the life of an astronaut in space. It is suited for children aged 7-12 years old. Players become astronauts, managing obstacles astronauts face on the moon.

The game addresses the Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer challenge by turning surviving challenges into gameplay. By optimizing one over the other in specific situations. Every action has consequences and every failure explains what went wrong.
details:
What it does & How it works:
Project Next Generation Astronauts is an interactive, browser-based survival game designed for children aged 7–12. Players take on the role of an astronaut stationed at the lunar South Pole. The core gameplay loop involves managing five resources: Power, Oxygen, Water, Food, and Crew Safety. Players must actively click on base modules—like the Solar Farm, Greenhouse, Water Recycler, and Airlock—to keep the base running. The objective is to survive for 30 days and collect 5 precious lunar samples while facing challenges like Solar Storm, Dust Storm and Water leaks.

Benefits & Intended Impact:
The project bridges the gap between complex aerospace engineering and early childhood education. Kids get to experience the consequences of space survival. If a player forgets the Airlock, they learn about the dangers of jagged lunar dust. If they ignore the Water Recycler, they learn about the 98% water recovery systems used on the ISS. This builds children's foundation on basic knowledge of space.

Tools & Languages Used:
The game was developed using a modern web stack. We used AI-assisted development tools (Lovable) to generate the game. We also used Deepseek for it to structure the game well and Github to transfer info on one account to the other.

Creativity & Factors Considered:
Our creativity shines through the "Friendly Sci-Fi" visual style—using Pixar-like 3D graphics and smooth, colorful UI to make space exploration feel fun for kids. We avoided instant "Game Over" screens. Instead, we implemented delayed consequences (like radiation building up over time) and educational failure screens that explain why the crew failed using real NASA facts. We made sure the game is simple and fun for a child to enjoy it.
